paper.title_en: Systematic characterization of argon and krypton-based Penning gas mixtures in a THGEM detector: Optimal concentration determination
paper.abstract_en: The Penning effect plays a crucial role in gas detectors by significantly enhancing ionization efficiency through optimized gas mixtures. Although this effect has been extensively studied in conventional detector configurations, its systematic characterization in Thick Gas Electron Multipliers (THGEMs) remains limited. In this work, we performed concentration-scan measurements on six Penning mixtures based on Ar and Kr (<math altimg="si259.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4544"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ar/CO</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>, <math altimg="si266.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4554"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ar/Xe</mi></math>, <math altimg="si271.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4559"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ar/DME</mi></math>, <math altimg="si276.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4565"><mi mathvariant="normal">Kr/DME</mi></math>, <math altimg="si281.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4570"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Kr/C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and <math altimg="si286.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4588"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Kr/iC</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math>) using a single-THGEM detector at pressures of 0.6 and 1.0 bar. The effective gain and energy resolution were systematically investigated as functions of the admixture gas concentration. The results show that, with the exception of <math altimg="si259.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4606"><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ar/CO</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>, all five remaining mixtures exhibit significant Penning effects. From the analysis of the gain curves, the admixture concentrations corresponding to the minimum THGEM operating voltage were determined for each gas mixture, ranging from <math altimg="si8.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4617"><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mtext>%</mtext></mrow></math> to <math altimg="si9.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4625"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mtext>%</mtext></mrow></math>. Among them, the optimal concentration of <math altimg="si30.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4633"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> in the <math altimg="si281.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4651"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Kr/C</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> mixture is about <math altimg="si12.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4670"><mrow><mn>0.3</mn><mtext>%</mtext></mrow></math>, consistent with previous measurements. The degree of gain enhancement due to Penning ionization in these mixtures depends specifically on the energy matching between the first ionization energy of the admixture gas and the excitation energy levels of the noble gas molecules. Based on the monitoring of discharge frequencies near the optimal concentrations for each mixture, the effective gains achievable at the same discharge probability can be quantitatively compared. Compared with pure Ar, the effective gain of <math altimg="si266.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4678"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ar/Xe</mi></math> is enhanced by more than a factor of 20 at the same discharge probability, while <math altimg="si276.svg" display="inline" id="d1e4683"><mi mathvariant="normal">Kr/DME</mi></math> shows an enhancement of about a factor of 40 compared with pure Kr.
